profile_sides — PROFILE measure op

• Data kinds: pairs → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.profile_sides(contour, n=101, normalise=True) (to call the implementation directly, import profileops; profileops.profile_sides(contour, n=101, normalise=True); from the registry, opsprofile.get("profile_sides"))

Usage

Extracts the upper and lower surfaces as functions of the chordwise coordinate. Returns a dict.

Divides the chord into n equal parts and, at each position, picks the upper and lower points where the contour crosses, by linear interpolation.

An open curve is rejected here -- if you pass a 1-valued (single-valued) function (such as an MTF curve), the lower surface cannot be obtained, so it fails explicitly, stating "this is not a closed section". This is guarded by validation, not by type (pairs is vocabulary used both for function data and for closed contours, so splitting the type would disconnect it from the existing contour-generating ops).

Returns:

dict: x ((n,)), upper / lower ((n,)), normalised.
